subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite product contracts, and the choice affects upgrade behavior for existing scheduled jobs and session retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted persisted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the strict-validation direction and rework or close this PR after documenting the user recovery path.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the new default only for newly created jobs and explicitly document that existing implicit jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted persisted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron store migration/default semantics and product compatibility, and path history shows recent ownership of the relevant cron store boundary.
